newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-JONSSON'S LATE GOAL SAVES SWEDEN.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-JONSSON'S LATE GOAL SAVES SWEDEN.

text.p: Jorgen Jonsson's late goal allowed Sweden to escape with a 1-1 draw against Latvia on Friday and preserved their unbeaten record in the ice hockey world championship.
Jonsson spoiled Arturs Irbe's shutout bid when he backhanded a shot between the Dallas Stars netminder's pads with 2:21 remaining.
His effort denied Latvia their first world championship win in 58 years.
The draw left Sweden on top of the pool B standings with seven points, one in front of the United States and two ahead of Canada.

Only the top three in each pool advance to the medal round so Latvia, playing in the world championships as an independent nation for the first time since 1939, are destined for the relegation tournament in Tampere.
For over two periods the game was an entertaining goaltenders duel with Irbe and Sweden's NHL netminder Tommy Salo of the New York Islanders trying to outdo each other.

Irbe, who arrived at the championships only on Thursday after Dallas had been knocked out of the first round of the NHL playoffs, provided the Latvians with the impressive goaltending which had been lacking in earlier matches.
Irbe showed no signs of jet lag as he continually frustrated the Swedish attack, stopping all but one of 35 shots fired at him.
Salo was almost as sharp at the other end of the ice, turning aside all but one of the 22 shots directed at him.
Igors Pavlovs broke the deadlock 1:27 into the third period, backhanding a rebound over Salo to put Latvia ahead.
